description: RFC 0008 stage 3: the L2 abstraction component (bigshark_abstraction) lifts the ordered action menu out of the solver behind a declared AbstractionId, and adds identity/lossy card bucketing. The component links only bigshark_poker (which itself brings no solver/IO dependency), and the lifted menu must reproduce the shipped solver abstract_actions element-for-element (test_abstraction_equivalence walks every reachable state of bounded heads-up games, including a DEEP-stack preflop root whose fractions produce interior targets, and compares the two with pinned node counts), so the end-to-end decisions are unchanged (replay 156/0/0). A golden identity digest pins the shipped default schedule so a wrong default fraction (including the preflop opener) cannot slip past the same-schedule equivalence harness. Every mutation below changes a menu/identity/bucketing semantic and must turn an abstraction test red. Recorded as 15 caught / 0 equivalent.

expected.rationale: test_abstraction (links the abstraction library) pins the state-neutral menu math (including a preflop opener with interior fraction targets), fraction validation (unreduced/non-positive rejection at both menu-build and declaration), the golden identity digest and exact shipped preflop fractions, deterministic identity with reduced-form normalization, typed refusal, the board-size fail-closed guard, and card-bucket layout with a witness for every hand category 1..9; test_abstraction_equivalence (links the solver) pins that the lifted menu equals solver abstract_actions on every reachable state with exact per-root node counts and a strictly-positive count of preflop INTERIOR nodes. Each mutation alters either the ordered-menu result the equivalence walk compares, the card-bucket layout/category the unit test enumerates, the golden digest/default, or the AbstractionId distinction/typed-refusal/declaration-guard the identity test asserts, so each changes a compared value or removes a required throw.

additional_targets.name: the shipped solver sizing vectors stay bit-for-bit identical through the adapter
